events.content:
Partial pre-rendering is now enabled and verified working — the build output shows the `/` route marked `◐ (Partial Prerender)`: prerendered as static HTML with dynamic server-streamed content. What I changed: - **`next.config.ts`** — added `cacheComponents: true`. This app is on Next.js 16.4 canary, where the old `experimental.ppr` flag is hard-deprecated (setting it throws an error); PPR was merged into the Cache Components feature and this top-level flag is the way to enable it now. No changes to the app code were needed. `app/page.tsx` already wraps `ProductList` and `Recommendations` in `Suspense` boundaries, which is exactly what PPR requires: the static shell (the `

Store

` plus the loading fallbacks) is prerendered at build time, and the two components' uncached `fetch` calls run at request time with their content streamed into the holes. One side note: `next build` auto-updated `tsconfig.json` (added `.next/dev/types/**/*.ts` to `include`) — a standard Next.js adjustment, safe to keep.
